selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What overall picture of the universe is presented at the beginning of this passage?
questions.answer: It is presented as a well-run realm, like an orderly kingdom or city where everything carries out its assigned role.

questions.question: What role do all things and species have in that dominion?
questions.answer: Each one carries out a specific assigned function.

questions.question: What do these many levels of ordered beings point to?
questions.answer: They point clearly to a single, all-encompassing rule and authority.

questions.question: What conclusion do these ordered ranks support?
questions.answer: They support the reality of one absolute sovereignty over all.

questions.question: What political examples are used to make the same point about divided rule?
questions.answer: The passage mentions two rulers in one land or even two local leaders in one area.

questions.question: What social examples are used to make this rule easy to understand?
questions.answer: The passage speaks of more than one ruler in one land or more than one local authority in one district.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from this universal order about any supposed partner in divine action?
questions.answer: There is no room for any partner to interfere in Allah’s governance.

questions.question: What inference is drawn from this broad and stable order?
questions.answer: No partner has any share in Allah’s governing actions.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention human weakness when discussing political power?
questions.answer: To show that if even frail people refuse rivals over a small authority, then absolute divine sovereignty would reject partnership even more.

questions.question: How does that example strengthen the argument about divine sovereignty?
questions.answer: It shows by comparison that absolute and sacred sovereignty would all the more reject partnership.

questions.question: What is the title of the truth discussed in this passage?
questions.answer: It is sovereignty.

questions.question: What image is used to help readers understand the structure of the cosmos?
questions.answer: The cosmos is compared to a prosperous kingdom or a well-governed city.

questions.question: What kinds of commands and laws are described as running through creation?
questions.answer: They are presented as commanding decrees, binding orders, and royal laws.

questions.question: What do these layered, obedient systems prove?
questions.answer: They prove a universal authority and absolute sovereignty.

questions.question: What is the relationship between absolute sovereignty and assigning partners to Allah in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage says true absolute sovereignty leaves no place for partners.

questions.question: How does the passage explain this through leadership examples?
questions.answer: It says even two rulers in one territory would ruin order and bring chaos.

questions.question: What evidence from the world counters the idea of multiple divine rulers?
questions.answer: The evidence is the visible harmony and regulation found everywhere in creation.

questions.question: What second argument against partnership comes from the nature of sovereignty itself?
questions.answer: Real sovereignty possesses honor and therefore does not admit equals.

questions.question: What example from human political behavior is used as an analogy?
questions.answer: Some people fight and even kill for small, temporary forms of rule.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about sharing in Allah’s rule, lordship, and divinity?
questions.answer: It is impossible because His sovereignty is sacred, real, and universal.

questions.question: What main claim does this passage make about authority in the universe?
questions.answer: It claims that all-encompassing authority belongs to Allah alone.

questions.question: What does the behavior of created things reveal about their place in that system?
questions.answer: They appear as obedient beings fulfilling assigned responsibilities.

questions.question: Why does the passage refer to armies across different levels of creation?
questions.answer: To show disciplined organization across the whole universe under one command structure.

questions.question: What does this pattern reveal about the ruler of creation?
questions.answer: It reveals one ruler with complete sovereignty and authority.
